texts.text: 1. What IBRANCE is and what it is used for
texts.label: text

texts.text: IBRANCE is an anticancer medicine containing the active substance palbociclib.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Palbociclib works by blocking proteins called cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6, which regulate cell growth and division. Blocking these proteins can slow down growth of cancer cells and delay the progression of your cancer.
texts.label: text

texts.text: IBRANCE is used to treat patients with certain types of breast cancer (hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative) which have spread beyond the original tumour and/or to other organs. It is given together with aromatase inhibitors or fulvestrant, which are used as hormonal anticancer therapies.
texts.label: text

texts.text: 2. What you need to know before you take IBRANCE
texts.label: text

texts.text: -if you are allergic to palbociclib or any of the other ingredients of this medicine (listed in section 6).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: -use of preparations containing St. John's Wort, an herbal product used to treat mild depression and anxiety, should be avoided while you are taking IBRANCE.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Talk to your doctor, pharmacist or nurse before taking IBRANCE.
texts.label: text

texts.text: IBRANCE may reduce the number of your white blood cells and weaken your immune system. Therefore, you may be at greater risk of getting an infection while you are taking IBRANCE.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you experience signs or symptoms of an infection, such as chills or fever.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You will have regular blood tests during treatment to check whether IBRANCE affects your blood cells (white blood cells, red blood cells, and platelets).
texts.label: text

texts.text: IBRANCE may cause blood clots in the veins. Tell your doctor, pharmacist or nurse if you experience signs or symptoms of blood clots in the veins such as pain or stiffness, swelling and redness in the affected leg (or arm), chest pain, shortness of breath or lightheadedness.
texts.label: text

texts.text: IBRANCE may cause severe or life-threatening inflammation of the lungs during treatment that can lead to death. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have any new or worsening symptoms including:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  difficulty breathing or shortness of breath
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: IBRANCE is not to be used in children or adolescents (under 18 years of age).
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are taking, have recently taken, or might take any other medicines. IBRANCE may affect the way some other medicines work.
texts.label: text

texts.text: In particular, the following may increase the risk of side effects with IBRANCE:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  Lopinavir, indinavir, nelfinavir, ritonavir, telaprevir, and saquinavir used to treat HIV infection/AIDS.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Clarithromycin and telithromycin antibiotics used to treat bacterial infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Voriconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, and posaconazole used to treat fungal infections.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: The following medicines may have increased risk of side effects when given with IBRANCE:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  Quinidine generally used to treat heart rhythm problems.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Pravastatin, simvastatin, atorvastatin, fluvastatin and rosuvastatin used to treat high cholesterol levels.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Sulfasalazine used to treat rheumatoid arthritis.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Alfentanil used for anaesthesia in surgery; fentanyl used in pre-procedures as a pain reliever as well as an anaesthetic.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Cyclosporine, everolimus, tacrolimus, and sirolimus used in organ transplantation to prevent rejection.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Dihydroergotamine and ergotamine used to treat migraine.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  Pimozide used to treat schizophrenia and chronic psychosis.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: The following medicines may reduce the effectiveness of IBRANCE:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  Carbamazepine and phenytoin, used to stop seizures or fits.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  St. John's Wort, an herbal product used to treat mild depression and anxiety.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while you are taking IBRANCE as it may increase the side effects of IBRANCE.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You should not use IBRANCE if you are pregnant.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You should avoid becoming pregnant while taking IBRANCE.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Discuss contraception with your doctor if there is any possibility that you or your partner may become pregnant.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you are pregnant or breast-feeding, think you may be pregnant, or are planning to have a baby, ask your doctor or pharmacist for advice before taking this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Women of childbearing potential who are receiving this medicinal product, or their male partners should use adequate contraceptive methods (e.g., double-barrier contraception such as condom and diaphragm). These methods should be used during therapy and for at least 3 weeks after completing therapy for females and for at least 14 weeks for males.
texts.label: text

texts.text: You should not breast-feed while taking IBRANCE. It is not known if IBRANCE is excreted in breast milk.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Palbociclib may decrease fertility in men.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Therefore, men may consider sperm preservation before taking IBRANCE.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Tiredness is a very common side effect of IBRANCE. If you feel unusually tired, take special care when driving or using machines .
texts.label: text

texts.text: This medicine contains lactose (found in milk or dairy products). If you have been told by your doctor that you have an intolerance to some sugars, contact your doctor before taking this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: This medicine contains less than 1 mmol sodium (23 mg) per capsule, that is to say it is essentially 'sodium-free'.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor or pharmacist has told you. Check with your doctor or pharmacist if you are not sure.
texts.label: text

texts.text: The recommended dose is 125 mg of IBRANCE taken once a day for 3 weeks followed by 1 week without taking IBRANCE. Your doctor will tell you how many capsules of IBRANCE to take.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you experience certain side effects while you are taking IBRANCE (see section 4 'Possible side effects'), your doctor may lower your dose or stop treatment, either temporarily or permanently. The dose may be lowered to one of the other available strengths 100 mg or 75 mg.

texts.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Contact your doctor immediately if you have any of these symptoms:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  fever, chills, weakness, shortness of breath, bleeding, or easy bruising which could be a sign of a serious blood disorder.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  difficulty breathing, dry cough or chest pain which could be a sign of inflammation of the lungs.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  painful swollen leg, chest pain, shortness of breath, rapid breathing or rapid heart rate as these can be signs of blood clots in the vein (which may affect up to 1 in 10 people).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Other side effects with IBRANCE may include:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Very common side effects (may affect more than 1 in 10 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Reduction in white blood cells, red blood cells, and blood platelets Feeling of tiredness Decreased appetite Inflammation of the mouth and lips (stomatitis), nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea Rash Hair loss Weakness Fever Abnormalities in liver blood tests Dry skin
texts.label: text

texts.text: Common side effects (may affect up to 1 in 10 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Fever with a drop in the white blood cell count (febrile neutropenia) Blurred vision, increased tearing, dry eye Alteration in taste (dysgeusia) Nosebleed Redness, pain, peeling, swelling and blistering of palms of hands and/or soles of feet (Palmar-Plantar Erythrodysaesthesia Syndrome [PPES]) Abnormal kidney blood test result (high level of creatinine in the blood)
texts.label: text

texts.text: Uncommon side effects (may affect up to 1 in 100 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Inflammation of the skin causing red scaly patches and possibly occurring together with pain in the joints and fever (Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus [CLE]).
texts.label: text

texts.text: A skin reaction that causes red spots or patches on the skin that may look like a target or 'bulls-eye' with a dark red centre surrounded by paler red rings (erythema multiforme).
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist, or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects, you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the bottle or blister and carton after 'EXP'. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
texts.label: text

texts.text: This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not use this medicine if you notice that the pack is damaged or shows signs of tampering.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.

texts.text: If you experience certain side effects while you are taking IBRANCE (see section 4 'Possible side effects'), your doctor may lower your dose or stop treatment, either temporarily or permanently. The dose may be lowered to one of the other available strengths 100 mg or 75 mg.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Take IBRANCE once a day at about the same time every day with or without food.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. Do not chew or crush the tablets. Do not split the tablets prior to swallowing. No tablet should be ingested if it is broken, cracked, or otherwise not intact.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you take more IBRANCE than you should
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you have taken too much IBRANCE, see a doctor or go to a hospital immediately. Urgent treatment may be necessary.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Take the carton and this leaflet, so that the doctor knows what you have been taking.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you forget to take IBRANCE
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you miss a dose or vomit, take your next dose as scheduled. Do not take a double dose to make up for the forgotten tablets.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not stop taking IBRANCE unless your doctor tells you to.
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you have any further questions on the use of this medicine, ask your doctor or pharmacist.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Like all medicines, this medicine can cause side effects, although not everybody gets them:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Contact your doctor immediately if you have any of these symptoms:
texts.label: text

texts.text:  fever, chills, weakness, shortness of breath, bleeding, or easy bruising which could be a sign of a serious blood disorder.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  difficulty breathing, dry cough or chest pain which could be a sign of inflammation of the lungs.
texts.label: list_item

texts.text:  painful swollen leg, chest pain, shortness of breath, rapid breathing or rapid heart rate as these can be signs of blood clots in the vein (which may affect up to 1 in 10 people).
texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Other side effects with IBRANCE may include:
texts.label: text

texts.text: Very common side effects (may affect more than 1 in 10 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Reduction in white blood cells, red blood cells, and blood platelets
texts.label: text

texts.text: Inflammation of the mouth and lips (stomatitis), nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea
texts.label: text

texts.text: Common side effects (may affect up to 1 in 10 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Fever with a drop in the white blood cell count (febrile neutropenia) Blurred vision, increased tearing, dry eye Alteration in taste (dysgeusia) Nosebleed Redness, pain, peeling, swelling and blistering of palms of hands and/or soles of feet (Palmar-Plantar Erythrodysaesthesia Syndrome [PPES]) Abnormal kidney blood test result (high level of creatinine in the blood)
texts.label: text

texts.text: Uncommon side effects (may affect up to 1 in 100 people):
texts.label: text

texts.text: Inflammation of the skin causing red scaly patches and possibly occurring together with pain in the joints and fever (Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus [CLE]).
texts.label: text

texts.text: A skin reaction that causes red spots or patches on the skin that may look like a target or
texts.label: text

texts.text: 'bulls-eye' with a dark red centre surrounded by paler red rings (erythema multiforme).
texts.label: text

texts.text: If you get any side effects, talk to your doctor, pharmacist, or nurse. This includes any possible side effects not listed in this leaflet. You can also report side effects directly via the national reporting system listed in Appendix V. By reporting side effects you can help provide more information on the safety of this medicine.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the blister and carton after 'EXP'. The expiry date refers to the last day of that month.
texts.label: text

texts.text: This medicinal product does not require any special temperature storage conditions. Store in the original blister package in order to protect from moisture.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not use this medicine if you notice that the pack is damaged or shows signs of tampering.
texts.label: text

texts.text: Do not throw away any medicines via wastewater or household waste. Ask your pharmacist how to throw away medicines you no longer use. These measures will help protect the environment.
texts.label: text
